derivedFrom: Intl.NumberFormat('vi-VN', {style:'currency', currency:'VND'}) on win32/x64, ICU 75.1, Unicode 15.1; ISO 4217 minor unit 0
description: Vietnamese money handling pinned as a contract between two ports. The formatting cases are read out of ICU, so they cannot be wrong in a way the platform itself would not be. The reading cases pin one of several published Vietnamese conventions and name the alternative they rejected; there is no platform to defer to, so the suite has to choose and say so.

currency.symbolNote: U+20AB VIETNAMESE DONG SIGN, as ICU writes it. U+0110 (Đ) and U+0111 (đ) are informal stand-ins
currency.groupSeparatorNote: vi-VN uses the same two characters as en-US with the opposite meaning: a dot groups and a comma separates decimals. Copying an en-US formatter here produces a wrong number that still looks fine.

readingConvention.fillerWhen: the hundreds are present, the tens are zero, and the units are not

unitOne.when: the units digit is 1 and the tens digit of the same triplet is 2 to 9

unitFour.when: the units digit is 4 and the tens digit of the same triplet is 2 to 9

unitFive.when: the units digit is 5 and the tens digit of the same triplet is 1 to 9

tensOne.when: the tens digit is 1, whatever follows it

emptyTriplet.rule: a zero triplet with a non-zero triplet below it reads as "không" plus its magnitude name; a zero triplet above the most significant one, or in the tail, is silence
emptyTriplet.example: 1000008 reads "một triệu không nghìn không trăm linh tám", while 1000000 reads "một triệu" and never "một triệu không nghìn"
emptyTriplet.alternative: other published conventions drop the magnitude name on the empty slot and read only "không trăm"

zeroHundreds.rule: a non-zero triplet whose hundreds digit is zero is read in full, so the "không trăm" slot is spoken -- but only when something of greater magnitude is also spoken, because then the position really is ambiguous
zeroHundreds.example: 1001 reads "một nghìn không trăm linh một", and 1000008 reads "một triệu không nghìn không trăm linh tám", while 5 reads "năm" rather than "không trăm linh năm"
zeroHundreds.alternative: a convention that reads every triplet in full regardless would say "không trăm linh năm" for five dong

readingConvention.reasonForTheCeiling: JS numbers are exact only to 2^53-1 and both ports take a number, so a larger amount would silently read a rounded value
